landing.header: There are Many Ways to Electrify
landing.headerDescription: Please register or sign in, then you will be prompted to tell us more about your specific requirements so we can recommend the appropriate equipment for your needs, identify incentives, and estimate cost savings. We can help with:
landing.fleetMessage: Compare the total costs of fleets of electrifying your fleet.
landing.workplaceMessage: Discover how much it costs to install chargers at your workplace.
landing.publicMessage: Compare the costs and revenue of providing public chargers.
landing.MUDMessage: Find out how much it costs to install chargers at multi-unit dwellings (MUD).
landing.alertMessage: Looking to replace your existing Fossil Fuel Fleet? See how much you can save by electrifying your fossil fuel fleet, available as a guest user

projectType.title: How Do You Want to Electrify?
projectType.subMessage: Choose a scenario and click Next to continue.

default.subMessage: We use this information to calculate fuel costs and applicable incentives.
default.organizationTypeTooltip: Your selection from this list will be used to determine incentive eligibility
default.projectLifetimeTooltip: Project lifetime is the amount of time you plan to operate the vehicles and/or charging infrastructure. This value is used to calculate your TCO analysis over the life of the project.
default.zipcodeTooltip: The zip or postal code of your project will be used to determine electricity pricing and potentially identify incentives.
default.justice40CommunityMessage: A Justice40 community, defined by President Biden's Executive Order 14008, is prioritized to receive at least 40% of benefits from federal investments targeting climate change and environmental justice. See community definition, and map data.
default.dacMessage: Zip code includes a disadvantaged community, eligible for additional state incentives. Check the box to indicate your site is within a disadvantaged community. Disadvantaged Community Qualifications
default.alertMessage: Increased incentive amounts provided for Justice 40 Community may vary by program and eligibility.

default.subMessage: Let's figure out how many chargers you will need. If you know exactly how many you will need, or you want to overwrite our recommendation, select the charger option. If you aren't sure, we can help you estimate using the spots you have available or the vehicles that need charging at your workplace.
default.alertMessage: Your charging needs will naturally adjust over the life of the project. We have provided a “Ports in 10 years” figure which adds a 5% growth in charging needs every year.

default.multipleVehiclesLabel: Multiple vehicles will share charger ports
default.multipleVehiclesTooltip: Selecting this option if employees will move their vehicles during the day so that multiple EVs can be charged using the same charger. Adds one vehicle per charger to your estimation. We will assume you need fewer chargers, and that you will do management.

default.subHeader: Choose the charger that best suits your needs. Level 2 is the most common and satisfies 90% of projects. Estimated charging times, prices, and outputs are included in each description to help you select the right option for you.
default.alertMessage: A generic charger has been selected based on your needs.

chargerSelection.level1Tooltip: Level 1 chargers can be plugged into a standard residential 120-volt (120V) AC outlet.
chargerSelection.level2Tooltip: Level 2 chargers use 240 volts, charge at over triple the speed of a level 1 charger.
chargerSelection.level3Tooltip: Level 3 chargers (or DCFCs) are the fastest EV chargers, and are typically found in commercial or industrial applications. The installation of level 3 chargers is much more complex and expensive than level 1 or 2.
chargerSelection.chargingTime1Tooltip: How long it takes on average to charge a vehicle to 100%. Assuming a <xx> mile commute a typical EV will require <yy:> kWh of charge.A <zz> kW charger will add this charge in <aa> hours and <bb> minutes
chargerSelection.equipPrice1Tooltip: The purchase price of electric vehicle supply equipment (chargers).
chargerSelection.installPrice1Tooltip: The price of installing chargers, including labor, trenching, materials, etc.
